utterances.text: Let me turn to your arrival in the town of Vitez, sir. I believe that was in early December of 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, actually, it was mid-to late November when I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you say that you set up the office of civil affairs next to the operations room of the headquarters of BritBat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Where was it before that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it had been around a corner, and it was a little bit smaller office, and by moving nearer the operations room it made me more accessible. And in contrast to my predecessor, I was a bit more senior and long in the tooth and with military experience, and so I think Colonel Williams understood that and felt a bit more comfortable in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You would agree that the situation confronting you when you arrived in Vitez in mid-November of 1993 was pretty grim; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely. It was like something out of World War II. Pretty grey and dismal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Most of the buildings that you saw in Vitez were marked -- pockmarked by shell fire or gunfire strikes; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a mix. In certain areas that had been predominantly inhabited by Muslims, those were pretty well destroyed, the roofs gone, and burned down. In areas in which it was obvious that there was a direct confrontation and fights going on, buildings were pockmarked on both sides, indicating that the building itself was a site of confrontation. In central Vitez, not that many buildings had been destroyed directly. Some had been subjected to long-barrelled automatic weapons from 50 calibre and above, markings from them and mortar rounds that would have been fired from Stari Vitez into central Vitez. In particular, Hotel Vitez had been hit many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And Hotel Vitez was the headquarters for the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The civil affairs office produced reports on a fairly regular basis; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: [Indiscernible] reports and weekly situation reports?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You gave some testimony concerning the linkage, if you like, to the provision of humanitarian aid to other concessions sought by the various factions to which a request was made. I'd just like to show you two exhibits on that, if I may: the first dated September the 1st, 1993, a report prepared by one of your predecessors, Mr. Rhodes, from the civil affairs office in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D124/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just a few brief questions on this document, sir. You can see in paragraph 2, your predecessor makes the observation that all sides have been guilty of using or denying the use of humanitarian aid, medical treatment, and supplies -- water, power, et cetera -- to further their military or political aims.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, and I made that statement also earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Right. If you turn over to the next page, there are some comments made or summarised in paragraph 5 made by Colonel Hadzihasanovic. Did you ever meet or speak with -- I think General Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On a couple of occasions, but most of my contacts tended to be, militarily, with General Alagic and his immediate staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That's general Mehmed Alagic; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. And one of his staff officers, Colonel Merdan.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Was General Alagic the commander of the 3rd Corps, headquartered in Zenica, while you were present in the area, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Affirmative.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Did General Alagic ever mention to you that the ABiH, insofar as Stari Vitez was concerned, had three options: the first to permit the Muslims within the Stari Vitez area to surrender; the second to permit them to be evacuated en masse to the southwest, and the third to keep them besieged and pressured so that ABiH supplies from Croatia would not be completely withheld?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he never directly made any statements of that nature to me. However, within BritBat, in discussions with BritBat, that was certainly mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. In your discussions with General Alagic, did he ever, on this subject, tell you that -- and I'm citing the book that he published in 1997 -- "Faced with this overall situation, we chose the last option. Instead of liberating Vitez, we chose to leave it as a strategic vent for the supplying of other parts of Bosnia"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'll take General Alagic at his word. I would say that both sides had an interest in a way of preserving Stari Vitez, because had the pocket not been there, then it would have probably made the Croatian pocket even more vulnerable to a mass attack from the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you. The point I was trying to elucidate was that the situation of the Muslims in Stari Vitez was considered by the 3rd Corps and that the deliberate decision was made essentially to preserve the status quo in order to ensure the continued supplies of materiel to the ABiH through Croatia. That was the view of your office and of your immediate neighbours, the BritBat contingent in Vitez; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A manipulation of the population in order to serve other interests, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And on the subject of -- well, I'll save that for later. You asked -- you were asked some questions about the Croat political party. The HDZ-BiH is the acronym that we use. Was that the acronym by which it was known when you were in the area, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It became more known or more properly addressed within our circles at BH-HDZ, but the same party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Whatever the acronym, it's the same party. Have you ever, with your political expertise, scrutinised any of the founding documents of that party, setting forth its basic constitution or elaborating its party political platforms throughout the years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in depth, but I have seen them. And I attended actually a -- I'm trying to think of the correct term. At the invitation of Mr. Kordic, a conference in Busovaca in 1994, and the precepts that were evidenced at that time and some of the documents that I looked through are, on the surface, very reasonable.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Speaking about the testimony that you gave regarding the comments assertedly made by Mr. Kordic concerning Muslims, would you agree with me that there is no record whatsoever in your contemporaneous journal about those comments, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, there is none in my journal. This is from recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Recollections of conversations that occurred in February of 1993, you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Over various occasions, and not just with Mr. Kordic but also with Mr. -- or, rather, General Roso, Mr. Valenta, and a few others.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: What was Mr. Kordic's position within the BH-HDZ prior to March of 1994, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Within the BH-HDZ?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a vice-president.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: How many vice-presidents were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Quite a few.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: He was just one of these vice-presidents; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you know what the powers of -- the prescribed powers of a BH-HDZ vice-president are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would depend upon the position within the party structure itself, and whether the individual would be operational on the ground or not, and what degree -- some of the designations of vice-presidents would be honorific in nature and others would be more functional in nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you derive this from the records and documents about which you've testified you regularly consult, or is this just your opinion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this was based upon not at the time but records reviewed by myself in my capacity within the U.N. liaison office in Zagreb subsequently, following up developments in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Would these be documents that were generated by the BH-HDZ itself, which actually delineated the specific powers of a vice-president, or military intelligence documents of the type that you regularly consulted concerning conclusions arrived at by others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A combination of both, taking open-source information and then cross-checking that against statements and interviews, discussions, that were held either personally or by other colleagues with individuals within the HDZ not only in Bosnia but in Croatia as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Who was the president of the BH-HDZ in Busovaca; do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The mayor of the city was Florijan Glavocic [sic], and I can't recall whether he was the president of the HDZ or not. I might have it in my notes. It's not something that I concentrated on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me put it to you, sir, that the mayor or the president of the HVO civilian government was actually Zoran Maric. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct initially, that's correct, and then Florijan took over after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Florijan Glavocevic was actually the head of the HDZ-BiH in Busovaca, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm trying to recall now. Yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You gave some testimony in connection with your initial meetings with Vitez politicians. Your first meeting, I believe, was within three or four days of your arrival in Vitez sometime in November of 1993, and you met with various local businessmen and politicians; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The meeting was chaired by Ivica Santic; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of the meetings, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And his actual formal title is not the mayor of Vitez, although that's a good vernacular --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Analogy, yes. The president.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The president of the HVO municipal government; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, you were instructed that Mr. Santic had occupied this position for the last six or seven months; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Isn't it true that he actually had been in that position for about two years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that's possible, but I hadn't been there for that period of time and I was taking information basically as presented by Luc Duchesne, and that would have covered the time that he was knowledgeable and that Randy Rhodes might have been knowledgeable.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that you told the prosecutors three years ago that you never, in fact, actually heard Mr. Santic say anything derogatory about Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't believe I said that, because I can certainly recall the anecdote that he told me about parachuting pork in to the Muslims, and that was maybe not the first or the second meeting but certainly within the first couple of months that I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Have you seen any reference to that comment in any of the daily reports or weekly situation reports that you prepared as the civil affairs officer of the United Nations in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I wouldn't have included that particularly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me just read you a portion of your statement from page 3, which says: "I never heard him, Mr. Santic, say anything derogatory about Muslims, although I do remember he used the pejorative term of 'balija' when describing Muslim people."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that's a pejorative term. It's negative.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Are we assisted by this argument? The witness has given his evidence about it. Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I believe that's correct, Your Honour. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just one question, though. You would agree that it's not unusual to refer in less than complimentary language to opposing forces when you're engaged in a civil war?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We don't need evidence on that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, speaking of Mr. Santic, he was responsible for running the civil government in the entire municipality of Vitez, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, administratively, in practical terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And in your dealings with Mr. Santic -- I think you said that you met him 30 times or so -- if issues relating to police, freedom of movement or security arose, he routinely referred you to Mr. Valenta, didn't he, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Valenta or to Mr. Kordic if it couldn't be solved basically at that level, although it tended to be a mix.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You said, on page 4 of your statement, that when dealing with Santic, "if certain issues were raised during discussion, we were always referred to Ante Valenta. By 'certain issues,' I mean issues such as the police, freedom of movement and security." That's what you told the prosecutors three years ago; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it's certainly the first call of recourse, but above him would have been Mr. Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You didn't make any contention to the prosecutors along those lines three years ago, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. And I believe that Mr. Santic later became the Deputy Minister of Energy in the government of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, and I had some meetings with him subsequently after that concerning the Bratstvo munitions factory and then independent of that in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: One of the other politicians that you met in Vitez was Pero Skopljak; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And in your view, you had determined that he was the leader of the HDZ party for Bosnia-Herzegovina in Middle Bosnia; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right, particularly for the Vitez area if -- in that particular area, and if -- my first line of recourse to getting anything done, if I couldn't get it done through Santic or Valenta, I also used or went to Mr. Skopljak to address various issues, to include one I can recall on freedom of movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Three years ago, you told the prosecutors that this gentleman was the leader of the HDZ party for Middle Bosnia; correct? Page 10.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't have the document, but if that's what it has. But I would focus it down more to the Vitez area. It's like you referred to Florijan being the leader for the Busovaca area. Mr. Skopljak would be more like for the Vitez area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: His function was to attach the party seal of approval required for higher-level decisions; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And indeed in your view, with your experience that you've derived over the years, the local political authorities in Vitez and Busovaca could do nothing without his assent, and that was always clear to you, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was one of the key actors, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You do agree that you say -- that you said on page 10, "It was always clear to me that the local political authorities would do nothing without his, Mr. Skopljak's, assent"; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's part of the formula, and Mr. Kordic would have been higher than Mr. Skopljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, but because these pages are not numbered, unfortunately, could you refer to the ERN reference number at the top that would give us the page number? The statement is not a numbered statement, as I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I would be delighted to do so, but the document that we've received does not have an identifiable ERN number on it. It actually only has numbers that go from D2490 -- it starts with D2940 and actually descends to 2480, and I was reading from page 2480.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That sounds like a Registry page. They do the things backwards. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. I just had trouble locating the particular passage, and perhaps if I could just get it from the number of pages from the last signature page, of the last page, that would help me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do you have a different one from the Registry?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: No, I have a differently numbered one. I'll make arrangements.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It's actually on the last page, third paragraph down, three lines from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, turning for a minute, sir, to Mr. Anto Valenta, what was his position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was designated as one of the vice-presidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Of what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of the -- well, initially when I met him, of the northern portion of the HR-HB, the Croat Republic of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I put it to you, Mr. Carter, that the Croat Republic of Herceg-Bosna did not have an office of vice-president. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's the way he represented himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I also put it to you that Mr. Valenta was one of three vice-presidents of the HVO and had been for some considerable time prior to your arrival; at least a year. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In fact, let me just show you a document. Maybe this will jog your memory, and since you say that you've looked at the official records that are in the public record. Just for the record, this is an October the 17th, 1992 decision appointing Mr. Valenta as one of the vice-presidents of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D125/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Have you ever seen this document before, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Did you know who the other two vice-presidents were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. This is before my time, and I would point out that this is before the republic was created in '93. And, of course, subsequent to the Washington Accords, it reverted back to the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It's not your testimony, sir, that the HVO was somehow abolished by the foundation of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna on August the 28th of 1993, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Are you aware of any information that would suggest to you that Mr. Valenta was not, in fact, or did not continue to be a vice-president of the HVO throughout the first five months of your tenure in the Vitez/Busovaca area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness can only deal with what he knows himself. He's given his evidence on the point. Now let's move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Who was the president of the HVO, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In our particular area or outside of our area?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The president of the HVO throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I couldn't say to that effect, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you know that Mr. Valenta was the HVO civil affairs representative throughout the Lasva Valley, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly, he was our primary point of contact and wielded some considerable authority, and deference was made to him partially because of his writings that he had done previously, which basically urged for cantonisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Were you aware that it was the view of the European Community Monitoring Mission that Mr. Valenta was the real number two in the HVO after Mate Boban?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. When was that allegation or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Don't bother.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you review any of the documents by Randy Rhodes, one of your predecessors, any of the reports prepared by him, insofar as they related to the political structures of the Croat authorities in the Vitez/Busovaca pocket, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not initially, no, because there had been a change in the battalions and a change in location, so some of the material -- well, many of the materials during his presence were not available, and so I had to rely to some extent initially, certainly, on Luc Duchesne's brief knowledge of the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. I take it, sir, that you did not have the opportunity to speak with Mr. Randy Rhodes directly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. He had already left, already departed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And the person to whom you did speak, Mr. Luc Duchesne, had only been in the area for a very short period of time; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, approximately four or five weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just to bring a conclusion to this line of questioning, you have not seen any of Mr. Rhodes' reports, I take it, subsequently.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have not, other than the one that you showed me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In that case, we can move on. Thank you. Did you know that Mr. Valenta still works for the government of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, I saw Mr. Valenta. I'm trying to recall, but I believe it was 1996 or 1997 in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, you gave some testimony concerning the chain of command within the HVO. Sir, it would be fair to say that as a former military man or as a military man with more than 25 years of experience, it was your view that Colonel Blaskic was able to exercise effective command and control over all HVO forces in the Vitez/Busovaca pocket, even down to the infantry company level; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, conventional units.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And how many soldiers are actually in an infantry company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it depends upon whose system you're looking at. Within the Yugoslav system, the Croatian HVO, approximately 100 men or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Whenever you met Colonel Blaskic, he always wore a rank badge of colonel on his breast pocket; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And also rank epaulettes on his sleeve too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On occasion, it would. Certainly a change when he went into black uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Was your first meeting with Colonel Blaskic on December the 15th, 1993, the date that you first met with Mr. Kordic too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't believe I met him any time prior to that, or if it was, it was an incidental meeting of no particular consequence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It would be true to say that following that meeting, you were in no doubt that Colonel Blaskic was indeed the commander of the HVO military forces in Central Bosnia; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You gave some testimony about the White Road Convoy. It would be fair to say that in that instance, as in all others, you were unaware of situations in which Colonel Blaskic's military orders were not carried out; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as conventional units were concerned and my knowledge basically during my time there, there may have been incidents, but generally speaking, his orders were carried out. We had a couple of incidents in which British troops were fired upon by Croatian HVO. They were fired back at, and we never had any repeated incidents of it. But I would say that's an anomaly rather than the norm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You never asked Colonel Blaskic whether there were any military units that were outside of his command, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I never deliberately asked him that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And, similarly, you never asked either Mr. Valenta or Mr. Kordic whether any military units were under the political chain of command, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I never did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Turning to the December the 15th, 1993 meeting that you gave some testimony about, it was Colonel Blaskic who actually did most of the talking at that meeting, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. Kordic was actually, sir, not in uniform at all, as you testified in your direct examination. Wouldn't you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm getting the dates confused, but at one point, that's correct. On the 21st of February at the Wolf's Lair, he was in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Not at the first meeting; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The mountain road via Guca Gora, about which you've testified the White Road Convoy ultimately travelled, that was territory controlled by the ABiH forces; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: One of the concerns articulated to you by Colonel Blaskic, and articulated on a fairly consistent basis after this first meeting, was the concern that convoys such as the White Road Convoy were being used to smuggle arms and ammunition; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And his concerns in this instance, at least, turned out to be justified because explosives, detonators, and ammunition were discovered being smuggled in that convoy; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In one of the vehicles, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That was despite the reassurances and representations made by ABiH commanders to you, amongst others; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, but it was never determined who placed the explosives in the vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And you say that the convoy proceeded without incident, without being attacked, to Zenica. On its return to Herzegovina, however, on December the 22nd, the convoy was attacked, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When it returned back into the Stara Bila and then the Gornji Vakuf areas, it was attacked, and I believe there were one or two Croatian drivers that were killed and injured -- or injured and killed, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That was actually the day that the ABiH offensive, the Christmas offensive, or just before Christmas of 1993, started; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And that was the offensive which resulted in the fatalities at Krizancevo Selo. I don't think you mentioned the number of people that were killed there, but it was about 75, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall the exact figure, but it was certainly a fairly high number. It was quite a confrontation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Were you actually present when the bodies of the people killed at Krizancevo Selo were dug up or exhumed three months later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. At the time of the White Road Convoy, sir, you were actually aware that the ABiH was actively planning offensive operations aimed at the Vitez/Busovaca pocket; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: UNPROFOR, BritBat, and myself had indications to suggest that they had intended an offensive. We made very strong representations to Dr. Lang and suggested to him that he must move his convoy immediately prior to the 22nd. He declined and did not leave until the 22nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you ever let Colonel Blaskic or anybody else within the Croat military leadership know that such an impending attack was about to be launched so that casualties could be minimised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it's not our role to provide information to one side or the other. But for humanitarian purposes, we attempted to let Dr. Lang know that it would not be in the interests of he or his convoy to remain there, and we made very strong representations to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me turn to the level of knowledge that you have about the structure of government within the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, sir. This entity had been in existence for two and a half months by the time that you arrived in Central Bosnia; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure of the exact date, but, yeah, for some bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you ever read the constitution of the Republic or the documents that set it up and defined the powers of its various organs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. If I recall correctly, the only constitution or founding documentation that I read had to do with the Croat Community and not with the Republic itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Were you aware that the supreme commander of the HVO armed forces, according to the constitution, was the president of the Republic, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The president of the Republic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mate Boban.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Prior to February the 14th of 1994, sir, could you just tell us what position, if you know, Mr. Kordic held within the government of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As one of the vice-presidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I put it to you, sir --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And self-styled, and in various documentations that I've seen, referred to as colonel in the HVO as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you ever ask Mr. Kordic, "What position do you hold within the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna," sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't, because that information was given to me by the British. I didn't ask him directly; that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Would it fair to say, sir, that there was some considerable confusion regarding the precise role of Mr. Kordic within the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, in your view, and also in the view of the British intelligence services; would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say that Mr. Kordic, as others, took on various guises and functions over the period of time, some of them evolutionary in nature, through promotion; some of them, as I was indicating in my testimony, there is a blurring of distinction and responsibility, particularly in times of conflict, where roles that are generally political in nature are -- sorry, military in nature are assumed by the military --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It's a very simple question. Isn't it true that there was a degree of doubt or confusion regarding Mr. Kordic's precise position within the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, in your view and in the view of your colleagues in the military community?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps there are -- I would suggest that there are others that perhaps have a clearer view than I might have, but some confusion in my mind, yes. Not necessarily confusion, but duplication of various responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, are you aware of anyone who just asked the question, "Mr. Kordic, what is your position within this new republic?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The question -- if Mr. -- or Brigadier Williams testifies, I'm sure he'll give you an answer in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Are you aware that he actually asked that question, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me put it to you, sir: Isn't it true that Dario Kordic was one of 69 legislators in the House of Representatives --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the assembly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes. In addition, the only appointments that he ever held were as the president of one of the commissions of the House of Representatives and a member of a ten-member commission on foreign affairs and internal security prior to February the 17th of 1992? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No -- well, not specifically, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you know that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But that would have been prior to 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, in 1994, or right at the end of 1993, the government of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna was appointed by the -- by the House of Representatives; did you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Who was the prime minister, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Why are we asking questions? It's not a school test.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm afraid that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness can't remember, probably, what happened six or seven years ago. If there is some point about it, Mr. Sayers, put it in terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That's fair enough, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm afraid my knowledge has waned with time, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That's all right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- and limited to the personal relationships that I might have had at the time with Mr. Kordic, Mr. Prlic, and some others.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Just before we go through these, and it won't take very long, did you make any contemporaneous notations in your diary as to who held what position when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have a legend that indicates at certain times when various individuals assumed various responsibilities, if I might refer to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Certainly, but let me just, in the interest of accelerating the pace of proceedings here, just suggest to you: Isn't it true that the prime minister of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna was Dr. Jadranko Prlic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and he also assumed the responsibility of foreign minister at one point, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Isn't it also true that there were ten separate ministries, each headed up by a different person, and Mr. Kordic wasn't one of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna held a major convention in, I believe, the city of Neum in February of 1994, and it was at that time that a gentleman by the name of Ivan Bender was appointed as the chairman of the House of Representatives, the legislative organ of the government; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And simultaneously with that appointment, Mr. Kordic and Mr. Vlado Santic from Bihac were appointed as deputy chairmen of the house of representatives; did you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not specifically, no. But I recall the incident about Mr. Bender.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And you would agree with me that before that, Mr. Kordic held no position within the government of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna of which you were aware; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in a formal status, except as reported to me by the British and information subsequently collected within the U.N. liaison office. One of the notations I have on page 44 is that Kordic is removed from military chain of command but remains deputy president of Herceg-Bosna, dated the 30th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But you have no personal knowledge whatsoever of the facts relating to that entry, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That information was provided to me by the British military intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I understand, sir, but you would agree that you are just reporting what other people have told you; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And another entry I have on the 21st of June, page 62, Kordic declared HDZ president.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Were you aware, Mr. Carter, that a presidential council of nine persons was established on December the 10th of 1993 by President Boban?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I can't honestly say that I would have --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- been aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Turning to Mr. Kordic for just a few moments, before the end of March of 1994, I believe that you had a grand total of three meetings with him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three that I have recorded. There may have been more, but I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. Kordic would routinely be present if anything of political significance was being discussed; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say, in a trans-Vitez or trans-Lasva Valley context, that's correct. I tended to try to relegate my contacts at the level appropriate; in other words, with the mayors or the political representatives of the specific area, whether it be Busovaca or Novi Travnik or Travnik or Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you know that before the civil war, that Mr. Kordic was a journalist and that he did not have a military background?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Were you aware that Mr. Kordic was elected as the president of the commission for the implementation of the Washington Agreement by the republic, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And it was in connection with his functions in that capacity that he made the requests to you for safe passage through Muslim-controlled areas to places such as Bugojno; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. The only time that you ever saw Mr. Kordic in camouflage clothing was the February the 7th, 1994, meeting about which you've testified; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it was the 21st of February. It was the one at the Wolf's Lair, that I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, reading from page 7 of your statement -- I don't think there is any dispute about this; it's page 2483 of the document we've been given. Relating to the 7th of February, 1994, meeting, you said, "I met Dario Kordic inside this building," which you've referred to as the Wolf's Lair. "He was in a camouflage uniform, although I do not remember seeing any badges or rank insignia on his uniform. It was the only time that I ever saw him in uniform." Does that refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was one incident; it was at the Wolf's Lair. I thought it was the 21st, but it might have been the 7th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: At this time, the ABiH was still in control of the portion of the main supply route just outside of Santici; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct. The HVO resumed -- resumed control of it sometime in late February, early March. I don't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Turning to the February the 21st meeting about which you've testified, the first comment made to you in that meeting was that the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna had its own laws, just as did UNPROFOR; and that comment was made to you by Mr. Kordic, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And Mr. Kordic said that notwithstanding his assurance to you that convoys -- U.N.-sponsored convoys should not be subject to physical inspections, that would have to be approved by the central government of the republic in Mostar; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. But he made the decision on the spot, at the end of the meeting. He assumed the responsibility himself, which is the appropriate decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And he specifically did so as a gesture of goodwill, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly that was the impact, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you or anyone of whom you know ever ask Mr. Kordic what the limits on his political decision-making powers were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. You gave some short testimony, and I won't spend too long on this, about meetings that you held with HVO commanders and HR-HB dignitaries on February the 25th of 1994. That was a meeting with Colonel Filip Filipovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And also present was General Ante Roso; correct? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vaguely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Were you aware that General Roso, unlike Mr. Kordic, was actually a member of the government of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna and that he also sat on the presidency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Turning to the Washington Agreement, this was negotiated in Washington, D.C., and signed approximately March the 14th or so of 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it was March the 1st, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: March the 1st? I may be wrong.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Early March.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. Kordic was not a participant in any of the negotiations on the Croat side, was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In fact, the Croat representative was an HVO vice-president by the name of Kresimir Zubak, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And he actually signed the Washington Agreement on behalf of the Croat contingent; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, and he subsequently assumed responsibility as the president of the Federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes. I have just one question in connection with the burned-down fuel station at the village of Divjak. That's a village that is to the south of another village called Grbavica; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say to the south and east, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes. Now, let me just conclude your examination, if I can, just by going over some of the opinions that we heard from you for the first time last night and this morning. With respect to the asserted rental of Bosnian Serb artillery and tanks, have you ever seen any receipts for that, any documentation that would support it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not either directly or indirectly within the U.N. These are reports that we had from both Zagreb and internally.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Suffice it to say, though, that neither you nor anybody else of whom you are aware ever spoke to any Croat commander who confirmed that; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No one that I know directly, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And the same is true with respect to Bosnian Serb army commanders, too; no one has ever confirmed that story to you, or anyone else that you know of. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not to me directly, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Were you aware -- just one question about the president of the HR-HB: Were you aware that the president, in addition to being the commander in chief of the armed forces of the HVO, also had the specific power to appoint and dismiss high-ranking military holders of office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It makes sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: With respect to the HV military police about which you testified very briefly, you didn't see any of these gentlemen yourself, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The -- yes, I did, as a matter of fact. In the -- in the store, the restaurant that was next to the burned-out garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: How many of them did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five. Five, six.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you ask them whether they were from Croatia or from Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I looked at their patches, and they were HV patches with "Policija" under it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right, but the question was: Did you ever ask them, either yourself or through an interpreter, where they came from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you speak Croatian yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I understand Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The last question, sir, with respect to Mr. Boban and his fortunes after the signature of the Washington Agreement, let me put it to you that he was actually one of 15 sector directors in the INA, and that the actual director of the INA -- and I think you know this -- was a gentleman by the name of Dr. Gregoric; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I wasn't aware of that specifically. I thought he was a director. But he was on the board of INA. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I ask the Court if tomorrow morning I could have ten minutes? Because it'll go beyond two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Really?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Just to clean up, it would -- I will keep it very focused, but I would ask just for ten minutes in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Carter, can you come back tomorrow? It'll be tomorrow afternoon, not tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's fine, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No more than --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- a few minutes. If you come back then, please, would you remember during this adjournment not to speak to anybody about your evidence, of course, and that includes members of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very well, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Half past 2.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: 1.00 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 9th day of November, 1999, at 2.30 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25
